D21·81w7 — 2026-10-10
chose: 2.3 coordinator: a lanes run (≥2) runs one loop that, each pass, gives every free lane (no live session, not parked) the first ready task no lane holds — in the lane holding its branch, else the next clean free lane — and runs each lane's session → gate → land → handoff as its own job. --max-sessions counts launches in flight; --cost-cap sums every lane's reported cost and is checked before each launch, so up to N-1 running sessions may add to it after it is reached. A stop rule that fires (needs_user, exhausted verify, an unlandable branch, stalls, a budget) launches nothing more and DRAINS: lanes in flight finish, are gated and file their handoffs, then run_stopped; the first stop wins. ^C or --stop signals every live session. Stalls count consecutively in completion order across lanes. A task_done is not credited for a task another lane held during the session. Concurrent launches resolve by the transport's session id; the timestamp fallback sees sibling sessions as candidates and stays unresolved rather than guess (session-driver D3). `--lanes 1` keeps the serial loop.
over: Killing in-flight lanes when a stop rule fires; N independent loops; counting only finished sessions against --max-sessions; folding rebase into 2.3 (a diverged branch still stops the run as error per D20 until 2.4's merge queue)
because: An in-flight lane's work is real and independent of the lane that fired the stop; killing it throws that away and leaves no handoff. Counting launches in flight is the only way --max-sessions stays a bound when N launch at once. The cost cap can only see what has been reported, so the overshoot is stated rather than hidden (session-driver D14 already scopes it to one driver).
